title: Procurement Risk Transfer & SLO Ladder — Dedicated Capacity Brief
body:
TL;DR: Buyers for Dedicated capacity care less about raw model accuracy and more about predictable throughput, clear failure-mode ownership, and the ability to shift operational risk to the vendor. This brief presents a procurement-facing narrative and a 3-tier SLO ladder that legal/procurement, platform, and SRE stakeholders can use to negotiate guarantees with minimal back-and-forth.

Audience and decision-makers
- Procurement / Legal: risk allocation, termination rights, credits, indemnities.
- Platform / Infra leads: throughput, burst behavior, autoscaling guarantees, resource isolation.
- Application engineering / ML infra: latency P95/P99, KV cache warmup semantics, model rollback process.
- Finance: unit economics, minimum commitment vs on-demand burst pricing.

Problem framing for customers (how we open the conversation)
- "We need ML endpoints that behave like a service: predictable capacity, measurable degradation, and clear remediation steps."
- Procurement translates this to: "Who owns which failures? When do credits kick in? Can we get isolation so noisy neighbors don't tank our latency?"

Core positioning pillars (short bullets to use in email/one-pager)
1) Predictable throughput: reserved GPU pools + configured baseline throughput with transparent burst policies.
2) Operational isolation: tenancy and network isolation options plus per-tenant scheduling to eliminate noisy-neighbor interference.
3) Escalation & remediation: documented playbooks, canary rollbacks, and dedicated support SLAs for resolved incidents.
4) Financial clarity: contract credits vs. true service-level availability; clear formula for credits tied to measurable SLOs.

3-tier SLO ladder (procurement-friendly, explicit triggers)
- Tier 1 — Bronze (Standard reserved):
  - Commitment: Baseline throughput allotment (tokens/sec) with 15% burst buffer.
  - Target latency: P95 <= 400ms for <512 token prompts under normal load.
  - Credit trigger: sustained (<72h) throughput below 90% baseline for rolling 30m window => credit = 2% monthly fee per hour over threshold, capped at 20%.
- Tier 2 — Silver (Enhanced isolation):
  - Commitment: Dedicated pools with soft isolation (affinity scheduling).
  - Target latency: P95 <= 250ms under baseline. P99 <= 800ms.
  - Credit trigger: any single incident resulting in >4 consecutive minutes of P95 > 2x target => credit = 5% per incident, escalation runbook and dedicated SE hours.
- Tier 3 — Gold (SLA-backed dedicated capacity):
  - Commitment: Hard isolation (pinned nodes / capacity reservation) and guaranteed throughput with pre-warmed KV cache for pinned models.
  - Target latency: P95 <= 150ms; P99 <= 350ms for specified model variants and sequence lengths.
  - Credit trigger: availability defined as ability to serve baseline throughput for 99.9% of billed minutes per month. Miss => financial credits up to 50% per month + right to terminate after repeated misses.

Notes on metrics and measurement (procurement will ask these)
- Measurement points must be vendor-observable and vendor/auditable. We propose: dedicated telemetry endpoints, daily SLO reports, and a monthly measurement CSV upload.
- Prefer percent-based credits (simple math) tied to clear windows and simple thresholds — avoids long disputes.
- Include option for third-party measurement during pilot for enterprise buyers.

Isolation semantics (short explainer for engineers + procurement)
- Soft isolation: affinity scheduling reduces cross-tenant interference but allows co-placement for efficiency. Good for cost-conscious buyers.
- Hard isolation: physical or logical node pins, strict network and scheduling controls; used where latency SLOs and compliance require full separation.
- Cache semantics: define "pre-warmed" (minutes/hours), warmup behavior (accepted cold-start rate during first X traffic), and associated credits if warmup not completed within agreed window.

Common buyer objections and suggested replies
- "We can run this ourselves cheaper." => "Self-hosting shifts sustained ops cost + headcount risk to you; our committed pools are optimized for utilization and include proactive kernel upgrades, security patches, and SRE on-call cover for peak incidents."
- "How do we know measurement is fair?" => "We publish telemetry, support joint audits in pilot, and use simple rolling windows with percent thresholds to keep disputes low."
- "What about model upgrades causing regressions?" => "Model rollouts are gated by canary traffic, automatic fallback to pinned model versions, and evaluation baselines that we include in the contract appendix."

Procurement checklist (for deal desk / AE to fill during negotiation)
- Baseline throughput (tokens/sec) per billing unit
- Acceptable burst size and frequency
- Isolation level (soft vs hard)
- Targeted model families, sequence length limit used for SLO calc
- Warmup commitments for pinned models, cache behavior
- Credit formulas + caps and termination rights
- Escalation contacts and on-call coverage windows
- Audit rights / telemetry export cadence

Sample negotiation script (short)
- AE: "Our Gold tiers give you node-level isolation and a 99.9% availability commitment for your reserved capacity — that translates into financial credits and the right to terminate if we fail repeatedly. Can we map your peak traffic shape to the baseline throughput number so we include an appropriate safety buffer?"
- Procurement: "We’ll want credits that scale and a clear third-party audit option for the pilot."
- AE: "Agree — we can offer a 90‑day pilot with joint telemetry access and a one-time audit scope. If the pilot meets targets, we move to your chosen SLO ladder."

Implementation considerations (notes for solutions engineering)
- Need playbook entries for: capacity over-commit allowances, burst throttling rules, model rollback SLA, and verification tests for warm cache.
- Default contract appendix templates should include a param table for: model family, baseline tokens/sec, billing multiplier, warmup minutes, P95/P99 targets, and credit formulas.

Open questions / TODOs
- Finalize numeric credit caps for Bronze vs Silver vs Gold (legal needs guardrails).
- Define third-party audit scope and cost-sharing model.
- Create a short pilot telemetry export package for procurement review.
- Validate abandonment/termination language with legal (what constitutes repeated misses?).

Appendix: Example credit calculation (worked)
- Buyer has Gold: monthly reserved fee = $100k; baseline throughput measured 720 hours; Availability miss = 0.5% below 99.9% (i.e. 0.005 * 720 = 3.6 hours missed). Credit = pro-rated up to monthly cap (we recommend 25% for example templates). In this case credit = $25k * (3.6 / 720) = $125. Keep math simple and defensible.

Quick references
- See CONF-1234 for technical SLO definition draft.
- Pilot telemetry package: github.com/redwood-inference/pilot-telemetry (WIP).

Notes to self: make a 1-page one-pager version of this for the sales kit. Also sync with legal on the Bronze credit cap by EOD next week.
